key_insight: Privileged Cross-modal Relational Distillation (PCRD) uses high-resolution 2D images during training to improve specimen-specific 3D microstructure reconstruction from lower-resolution volumetric imaging alone.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on expensive high-resolution 3D imaging when characterizing fiber architecture in carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites.
method: Use scanning electron microscopy as the privileged training modality and micro-CT as the inference input.
Transfer spatial organization by matching teacher–student similarity distributions around corresponding spatial anchors.
Avoid direct alignment of heterogeneous feature vectors.
evidence_signal: In pultruded carbon fiber composites, PCRD improved 2D mAP by 1.66 percentage points over direct micro-CT training and matched 89.97% of reference fiber centerline length in independent synchrotron CT validation, versus 75.08% for the interpolated low-resolution volume.
watch_item: Training requires corresponding spatial anchors across modalities, and generalization beyond the demonstrated composite system remains unestablished.
paper_title: Learning from high-resolution 2D images to reconstruct 3D microstructures
